clue.text: A word of twenty-six letters

parts.note: pretends to describe one enormously long word, but means the single name for the whole set of letters from A to Z

explanation.surface: A puzzle about some impossibly long word of twenty-six letters.
explanation.walkthrough: One expects a long word; instead the 'word' is the collective term that contains all twenty-six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The English letter set from A to Z numbers twenty-six, and the term for that full set is this.

clue.text: Persuade to believe dog's ready for walkies

definitions.meaning: to deceive someone into believing something untrue
a dog wearing its lead, set for a walk

explanation.surface: A dog owner coaxing their pet into believing it is time for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to deceive or string along, and literally a dog with its leash attached.

clue.text: Meteorologists enjoy these feelings of elation

definitions.meaning: weather forecasters track areas of high pressure, which bring fine weather

explanation.surface: Weather forecasters relishing their moments of joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticyclones are weather-map pressure systems, and the same plural noun means peaks of euphoria.

clue.text: Harbottle is thrown out by union

indicators.note: thrown out suggests the name Harbottle is disordered and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Harbottle is being expelled by a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' looks like a trade union but is a marriage pledge; 'thrown out' rearranges HARBOTTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a promised marriage, a union of two people.

clue.text: Cry when people meet

parts.note: reads as a greeting, but hints at the hunt's meet, the gathering of riders, and the shout raised when the fox is seen

explanation.surface: A greeting shouted when friends get together.
explanation.walkthrough: In British fox hunting, a 'meet' is the gathering of the hunt; the huntsman's shout on sighting the fox is this cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional fox-hunting shout given when the quarry is spotted by the riders.

clue.text: Release will be subtle with later time

indicators.note: later says the letter for time is placed further on in the word subtle

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark about how a release will become subtle with time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'later' moves the T of SUBTLE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease out a property one is renting oneself is to release it to another tenant.

clue.text: Upset, having to switch arrangement

indicators.note: switch tells us to swap the letters of upset into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone upset at having to change their plans.
explanation.definitionFit: A configuration or organised system of things is an arrangement.

clue.text: Diabolical service!

parts.note: sounds like a complaint about terrible service, but means a worship ceremony for the Devil

explanation.surface: A customer exclaiming about awful service in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diabolical' means dreadful in casual British use, but literally devilish; 'service' is a church rite.
explanation.definitionFit: A Satanic ritual parodying the Christian Eucharist is literally a devilish church ceremony.

clue.text: Technician in control

definitions.meaning: a skilled person who designs or maintains machines
as a verb, to manipulate or contrive an outcome

explanation.surface: A technical expert sits in the control room.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a skilled mechanic; as a verb it means to contrive or steer events.

clue.text: Trapped and dismissed as a batsman

definitions.meaning: in cricket, out when a fielder takes the struck ball before it bounces

explanation.surface: A cricketer feeling trapped after being given out.
explanation.definitionFit: Means captured, and is also a cricket dismissal where a fielder holds the ball on the full.

clue.text: Head initially greatly put out by state of apathy

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbance, so the letters are mixed up
initially means take only the opening letter of head

explanation.surface: A boss greatly annoyed by a mood of indifference in the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes H from Head; 'put out' rearranges H with GREATLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish torpor and lack of energy is a condition of apathy.

clue.text: Boss organised Conservative bid for sympathy

indicators.note: organised indicates the letters of boss are arranged afresh

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A boss rallying a Conservative campaign to win public sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale of woe told to elicit pity is an attempt to gain sympathy.

clue.text: Jabbing petty officer with ruler

parts.note: PO is the naval abbreviation for petty officer
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A naval officer and a monarch prodding each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodding with a finger or stick is jabbing.

clue.text: Serve alcohol mixes for one no longer in form

indicators.note: mixes suggests stirring the letters of the phrase into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A barman serving drinks to someone past their best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in form' sounds like sporting fitness, but a form is a British school class; 'mixes' rearranges SERVE ALCOHOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has finished secondary education no longer belongs to a school class, called a form in Britain.

clue.text: Religious rite holds a thousand in strange trances

indicators.note: in tells us the pair of letters goes inside the jumbled word
strange tells us the letters of trances are rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A religious ceremony involving a thousand people in odd trances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges TRANCES into SACRENT; 'in' places A and M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism or the Eucharist is an example of a formal Christian ceremony.

clue.text: Decline to join ring with women supporting fiction, and remain uncultured

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed beneath the other piece

parts.note: a lie is a fiction
to fall is to decline
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Instructions to decline a ring, with women backing a story, and stay unrefined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncultured' here means not cultivated, as with farmland left unplanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmland left unplanted for a season stays uncultivated, a playful sense of uncultured.

clue.text: Foreigner satisfied his appetite only to lose friendship

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner
he ate

explanation.surface: A visitor from abroad eats his fill and then falls out with his hosts.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to make them turn away, so the friendship is lost.

clue.text: Obstruct mail in capitals

parts.note: to block is to obstruct
letters are mail

explanation.surface: Someone holding up post in the nation's capital cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capitals' looks like cities but means uppercase writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain uppercase writing, as demanded on forms, is in capitals.

clue.text: Came to the point: red tape requires a new order

indicators.note: a new order tells us to rearrange the letters of red tape

explanation.surface: An official finally gets to the point: bureaucracy needs reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came to the point' sounds like speaking plainly, but means narrowing to a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Something narrowing gradually to a sharp end has come to a point.

clue.text: Judge the fools will accept direction

indicators.note: will accept means the fools take in the next letter

parts.note: asses are fools
S is the compass direction south

explanation.surface: A judge warning that the idiots will accept being told what to do.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaluate or appraise something is to judge it.

clue.text: Exist with just a part interest

parts.note: to be is to exist
a half is only part of something

explanation.surface: Someone who has only a partial stake in a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting for someone means acting in their interest, as in 'on behalf of'.

clue.text: Destined, we hear, to be honoured

indicators.note: we hear means the word for destined is heard rather than written

parts.note: fated means destined

explanation.surface: Someone destined to be honoured, or so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound alike in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Being celebrated or lavishly entertained is being honoured.

clue.text: David and Sam split change

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Two men named David and Sam split their spare change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'David' looks like a man's name in the story, but King David is traditionally credited with writing the Psalms; 'change' is the signal, not loose coins.
explanation.definitionFit: King David is traditionally held to be the composer of the Psalms.

clue.text: The art of spelling

parts.note: suggests orthography, but means casting spells, as wizards do

explanation.surface: A description of the skill of writing words correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' is the casting of spells, not orthography.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery and wizardry are the craft of casting enchantments.

clue.text: Scholar more tidy in crocodile, for example

parts.note: MA is the abbreviation for Master of Arts, a scholar
neater means more tidy

explanation.surface: A tidier scholar in a crocodile, a British line of schoolchildren walking in pairs.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'crocodile' is also a line of children walking two by two, which the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile is an example of a predator that will kill and eat humans.

clue.text: Sounds like a tugboat, but isn't

definitions.text: Sounds like a tugboat, but isn't

parts.words: Sounds like a tugboat, but isn't
parts.note: the name rhymes with a word for a towing vessel, yet it is a small sailing boat

explanation.surface: A remark that some vessel's name resembles a tugboat.
explanation.walkthrough: The name rhymes with 'tugger' but means a small sailing vessel with lugsails.
explanation.definitionFit: A small two- or three-masted fishing vessel rigged with lugsails, rather than a towing craft.

clue.text: Built a home for good man in want

indicators.note: in says the saint goes inside the word for want

parts.note: to need is to want
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: A good man in need who built himself a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that have made a nest have built a home.

clue.text: County players dejected

parts.note: Down is a county in Northern Ireland
a cast is a company of actors

explanation.surface: A county team's players feeling dejected after a loss.
explanation.walkthrough: DOWN is a county of Northern Ireland; a cast is the players in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low or crestfallen is being dejected.
